chapter: Miles Davis stories and what jazz means
title: Sister Rosetta Tharpe, the Golden Gate Quartet and gospel in popular music
summary: Gil recalls Tharpe singing gospel in clubs, and says Ray Charles brought gospel into popular music.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: Well I guess we could sort of pick up loose ends here. You were saying something absolutely fascinating about (Sister Rosetta Sharpe?) Tharpe a minute ago when we were off the air, if you want to put it that way. I think that's worth mentioning. You were talking about the kind of thing she was doing thirty years ago.
She was yes. Twenty years ago. Twenty five years ago I'd say she was doing it.
And how would you describe it?
She was singing regular gospel numbers, you know. In clubs.
And so you're saying she was one of the innovators in doing them?

............ in the clubs. I imagine a lot of people put her down for that. She probably had trouble with old folks who thought that she shouldn't be doing that in clubs. She had a lot of hit records on Decca (popular tunes?) like popular gospel you know. But then it took a long time to finally break through. Ray Charles, I guess, did it really in a way. He (got an enormous audience
singing the gospel in the popular music you know. Singing that style and using popular songs. Rock and roll...
So you think that those two are especially among the innovators, is that what...
And then of course he added to the Western, the Country Western to his, or picked that up or whatever that is.......
Well that was, they made those records, it was called that, it wasn't really that. Just a bunch of old, there weren't too many good tunes on those I don't think. I loved 'You Are My Sunshine'.

Yes. (LAUGHTER). That brings something else to mind and that is the whole business, I guess one might almost ask the question now, what is jazz? Because it's going through it seems to me, or has gone through ...........
I happened to remember, now Sharpe Sister Rosetta sang with a quartet. She had a male quartet with her. I can hear the record now. I remember that. Do you remember the 'Golden Gate Quartet'?
Yes, I do, yes I do.
Well, she had a group like that.

They were the very first ones too. Everybody loved them too. It just had to be a break through finally because you could tell every time the Golden Gate Quartet came on every body was crazy about them. You know, and rightfully so. They came to Hollywood and they were in some musical............ (VOICE FADES OUT). sang a Harold Arlen song. Oh, they were great.
I remember in those days we were madly in love with them, in those days. But (I want to ask?) this whole question of the change in jazz style. I wonder if you.....
